questions.stem: Intra tubular germ cell neoplasia is implicated as a cause for the following testicular tumour?
questions.solutionHtml:
Seminomas
  • Intratubular germ cell neoplasia (ITGCN), also known as carcinoma in situ of the testis, is a precursor lesion to invasive germ cell tumours, especially seminomas.
  • ITGCN is characterized by malignant germ cells confined to the seminiferous tubules, without invasion into the surrounding tissue.
  • ITGCN is believed to be the precursor lesion to 50-70% of cases of classical seminoma.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 694

questions.stem: All the following are testicular dysgenesis syndromes except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Epispadias
  • Epispadias is not a testicular dysgenesis syndrome.
  • It is a congenital anomaly where the urethra opens on the dorsal side of the penis due to incomplete fusion of the urethral folds.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 694,696

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most common testicular tumour seen in children?
questions.solutionHtml:
Yolk sac tumour
  • Yolk sac tumour is the most common testicular tumour in children, accounting for approximately 60-80% of cases.
  • This tumour is typically seen in children younger than 3 years of age and is characterized by the presence of Schiller-Duval bodies on histology.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 695

questions.stemHtml: Histopathological findings of a testicular tumour are shown below. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Endodermal sinus tumour
  • The given histopathological image shows Schiller-Duvall bodies which is a characteristic feature of endodermal sinus tumour, also known as yolk sac tumour.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 695

questions.stem: All are germ cell tumours except-
questions.solutionHtml:
Leydig cell tumour
  • Leydig cell tumour is not a germ cell tumour, but a sex cord-stromal tumour of the testis. It arises from the Leydig cells, which produce testosterone.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 695,696

questions.stem: Microscopic features of seminoma include all of the following except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Gland formation
  • Seminoma does not show gland formation, but instead, it causes the destruction of the seminiferous tubules.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 695,696

questions.stem: Tumour marker for Endodermal Sinus Tumour:
questions.solutionHtml:
Alfa fetoprotein
  • Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is a tumour marker that is commonly elevated in patients with endodermal sinus tumours, also known as yolk sac tumours.
  • Elevated levels of AFP may also be seen in other types of germ cell tumours and certain liver diseases.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 695,696

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a risk factor for developing testicular carcinoma?
questions.solutionHtml:
Benzopyrene exposure
  • Benzopyrene exposure is a risk factor for other cancers, such as lung cancer and skin cancer, but not for testicular carcinoma.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 697,698

questions.stem: The commonest site for extragonadal germ cell tumour is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Mediastinum
  • The commonest site for extragonadal germ cell tumour- Mediastinum
  • It is usually seen in Klinefelter syndrome.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 697,698

questions.stem: Infertility is a common feature in “Sertoli cell only” syndrome because -

options.label: A
options.text: Too many Sertoli cells inhibit spermatogenesis via inhibin

options.label: B
options.text: Proper blood-testis barrier is not established

options.label: C
options.text: There is no germ cell in this condition

options.label: D
options.text: Sufficient numbers of spermatozoa are not produced

questions.answerText: There is no germ cell in this condition
questions.solutionHtml:
There is no germ cell in this condition
  • Sertoli cell-only syndrome (also known as germ cell aplasia) is a condition in which there are no germ cells (sperm-producing cells) present in the seminiferous tubules of the testes.
  • This leads to infertility because sperm cannot be produced in the absence of germ cells.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 697,698

questions.stem: Which testicular tumour is the most common in adults among the following Options:
questions.solutionHtml:
Seminoma
  • Seminoma is the most common type of testicular tumour in adults, accounting for about 40-50% of all cases.
  • Most common testicular tumour in infants–YST
  • Most common testicular tumour in adults- seminoma
  • Most common testicular tumour adults–Lymphoma


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 697,698

questions.stem: A patient with a right-sided testicular tumour is being evaluated for metastasis. Which group of lymph nodes is most likely to get involved first?
questions.solutionHtml:
Inter-aortocaval nodes
  • Inter-aortocaval nodes are the first group of lymph nodes that receive lymphatic drainage from the testes and thus are the most likely to be involved in metastasis from a right-sided testicular tumour.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 697,698

questions.stem: Testicular involvement without epididymitis is a feature of-
questions.solutionHtml:
Syphilis
  • Testicular involvement without epididymitis is a feature of syphilis.
  • It is known as syphilitic orchitis and is a rare manifestation of syphilis.
  • It is usually seen in the late stage of the disease and can present as a painless enlargement of one or both testes.
  • Other features of late syphilis include gummatous lesions, neurosyphilis, and cardiovascular syphilis.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 697,698
